children: A Reference Field pointing at a missing or unpublished target — computed at read time and surfaced as a Phantom Node; four were found in real prod data.

A Dangling Reference is a reference whose target no longer resolves: the referenced Document was deleted, or it exists but isn't published (and Graph Traversal is published-only). The pointer still sits in the referrer's payload — the data isn't corrupt, the target is just gone.

blocks.text: Why it never lives in the table

children: to_id in the Content Edges Table is a foreign key, so a dangling edge

. The Edge Projector simply never writes it. That means dangling-ness is not a flag on a row — there is no dangling column anywhere. It is derived: when traversal expands a referrer and the target won't resolve, it materializes a Phantom Node on the spot.

This read-time derivation is the key design choice. The write side stays clean and FK-safe; the read side does the honest accounting. A Reference Field that is arrayOf can dangle in just some slots — each unresolved slot becomes its own phantom.
dangling references were found — small, but exactly the kind of quiet referential rot that Blast Radius exists to prevent and that the Graph View now makes visible.
